scopePolicy.summary: Scope is a DENYLIST, not an allowlist. Every first-party .sol file in a submodule is IN SCOPE by default — including brand-new files that appear in a code change — UNLESS its path matches the denylist below. This honours Law 1 (recall beats report-tidiness): a contract is never silently dropped from a scan. Noise is removed at triage (via /ledger), not by withholding the scan.
scopePolicy.denylistRationale: Only the project's own nested lib/ (third-party + forked dependencies) is excluded by default, because per C4 'issues in parent/forked contracts where root cause is OOS' are handled at the findings layer (sanitizer / validity-checker), not by skipping the file. test/, script/, src/interfaces/, mocks/, and any new first-party .sol are all IN SCOPE.
scopePolicy.perProjectArrays: Each project's `scope` / `scopeFocus` / `scopeContext` arrays are ADVISORY FOCUS HINTS and historical snapshots — they are NOT the in-scope gate and must never be used to exclude a changed first-party file. A project's `outOfScope` array may add EXTRA human-chosen exclusions on top of defaultDenylist, but the only baked-in exclusion is `lib/**`.
scopePolicy.newFileHandling: Any first-party .sol that changed since lastAuditedCommit but is absent from the stored `scope` snapshot is a NEW-IN-SCOPE file: it is pulled into the scan automatically and surfaced loudly in the run summary (never dropped, never gated behind a confirmation step).

Nested submodules (flax-token, pauser, reflax-yield-vault) are phoenix projects tracking master HEAD; openzeppelin-contracts v5.6.1 and forge-std v1.16.1 are external pins. solc 0.8.28.
stable-staker.knownIssuesSource: lib/stable-staker/CLAUDE.md (project documentation). README.md is a generic Foundry template with no Scope/Known-Issues section; no dedicated scope.md or known-issues.md exists. Items below are design decisions / invariants extracted from CLAUDE.md.
knownIssues: Core emission-cap invariant by design: no sequence of user actions can mint more than phUSDPerDay per token over any window; _updatePool is the only writer of accPhusdPerShare, folding in exactly elapsed * phusdPerSecond per update
Integer-division dust always rounds DOWN (in protocol's favor); empty-pool windows accrue nothing; flash staking earns nothing - by design
phUSDPerDay settles the pool at the OLD rate before changing it - by design

Yield stays protocol-owned: stakers only ever get principal back plus phUSD emissions; accrued strategy yield accumulates as protocol-owned surplus (skimmed via strategy's skimSurplus). The farm never reads totalBalanceOf to credit a user

Exits forward the ACTUAL received amount (balance delta) while internal principal accounting is decremented by the REQUESTED amount; sub-amount differences remain protocol-owned yield/loss (consistent with ERC4626YieldStrategy rounding rule)

Underwater withdraw block: while a token's strategy is below par (totalBalanceOf < principalOf), withdraw reverts (StableStaker: strategy underwater) so non-migrating users aren't forced to realise a loss. emergencyWithdraw and migrateOut are intentionally NOT blocked - the escape hatch and migrations accept the haircut
Replacing an in-use yield strategy does NOT auto-migrate funds out of the old one - operator must drain it first or replace only while totalStaked == 0 (documented operational requirement)

Owner trust assumptions: owner controls addToken, phUSDPerDay emission budget, setPauser, setMigrator, setYieldStrategy - centralization by design. Migrator is a permissioned role (migrateOut/depositFor callable only by configured migrator)
Behodler3 pausing via pauser/IPausable; permissionless emergencyWithdraw escape hatch is callable even while paused, by design
designDecisions: MasterChef accumulator model: accPhusdPerShare + rewardDebt, per-token pools with owner-set phUSDPerDay emission budget
Rewards minted on demand (not pre-funded); contract is an authorized phUSD minter
Per-token EnumerableSet of stakers (getStakers / getStakersRange / stakerCount)

Opt-in per-token yield routing via setYieldStrategy(token, strategy); address(0) means idle-hold. All five principal-moving paths (stake, withdraw, emergencyWithdraw, migrateOut, depositFor) route through the strategy when set
setYieldStrategy forceApproves the strategy for unlimited token, sweeps existing idle balance into it, and resets the old strategy allowance to 0 on replacement/clear
Strategy wiring requires both sides: strategy.setClient(staker, true) by the strategy owner AND staker.setYieldStrategy(token, strategy) by the staker owner
withdrawDisabled(token) public view returns true while withdraw is blocked (false when no strategy set)

phoenix-nft-staking.knownIssuesSource: lib/phoenix-nft-staking/CLAUDE.md (rewritten in story-008, commit 3087b8e). No dedicated Known Issues / Out of Scope / Limitations section exists; design decisions and invariants below were extracted from the Feature Specification and Critical Invariants sections.
knownIssues: Owner trust assumptions: owner controls setTargetAPY (bounded by MAX_TARGET_APY = 0.5e18), setDispatcherIndex, setNFTMinter, setDispatcherHook, setStakedId, topUp, pullAndRefresh - centralization is by design
Pauser trust assumptions: a designated pauser address (via global Pauser/IPausable) can pause/unpause user-facing state-changing functions

setStakedId / setDispatcherIndex / setNFTMinter only callable while totalStaked == 0 - this is intentional to prevent mid-stake reconfiguration from swinging APY math; do NOT flag the empty-pool guard as a DoS
setDispatcherHook has NO empty-pool guard - hook rotation is intentionally a live operation

emergencyWithdraw forfeits pending reward, skips _syncBudget/_updatePool, and is callable while paused - by design as escape hatch for ID-change migrations or broken dispatcher hook / NFT minter / recompute path
topUp does NOT call _syncBudget - intentional to preserve dispatcher-hook-independence
Floor rounding via OZ Math.mulDiv used throughout reward math - conservative-for-protocol is intentional
Edge cases totalStaked == 0 || targetAPY == 0 || price == 0 collapse rewardRate R to 0 - by design (zero-APY is a supported pause-emissions mode)

APY-as-floor semantics: per-NFT effective APY for the most-recent minter equals targetAPY exactly; earlier minters who paid latestPrice / r^k earn targetAPY * r^k > targetAPY (geometric-growth multiple). Lone staker earns targetAPY (or geometric multiple), NOT N * targetAPY - there is no participation multiplier. This was the audit M-03 fix (sizing R against the staked subset S = totalStaked * latestPrice rather than aggregate minted notional T)
Late stakers never get retroactive rewards - accRewardPerShare advances only between lastRewardTime and block.timestamp

Emissions stop cleanly at windowEnd; recompute pushing windowEnd forward after depletion is not retroactive (prior accrual settled first via _updatePool capping elapsed at min(now, windowEnd) - lastRewardTime)

ScheduleRecomputed event: on-chain field name totalNFTValue is preserved for off-chain consumer compatibility but its meaning shifted in audit M-03 from aggregate T to staked-subset S = totalStaked * latestPrice - do NOT flag as misleading naming

Single active token ID per staker contract (one staker per NFT at a time) - cross-ID leakage is structurally impossible by design; no in-contract whitelist, no per-ID mapping, no allocation-point math

_safePay reverts on shortfall rather than silently capping payouts; wei-level dust escape into rewardBudget when per-user pending floor-rounding marginally exceeds cumulative _updatePool increments is intentional

ACCEPTED TRADE-OFF (owner, 2026-07-25) - DO NOT REPORT: same-denomination nudge arbitrage in BatchNFTMinterMultiToken. The payment token is DELIBERATELY PERMITTED to be a nudge-whitelisted token (docs/phoenix-nft-staking-payment-token-as-nudge-token-plan.md). Consequence: the qualifying cost and the reward are denominated in the same asset, so `pot > nudgeSize * price` is arithmetic any bot can evaluate in one eth_call, and the pot will be taken promptly whenever it exceeds the qualifying cost. This is intended and is the contract's own stated position (:62-70): 'the pot is by construction a fraction of the cost of the nudgeSize mints required to qualify - every claim is net-positive for the protocol. If someone over-funds this contract beyond the mint cost and a bot snipes it, that is still correct behaviour; the error was in the sender.' Making the arithmetic legible does not change the economics. Do NOT file 'batching is profitable', 'the pot is sniped by MEV bots', 'payment token should not be whitelisted as a nudge token', or 'setNudgeTokenWhitelist no longer rejects the payment token'. SCOPE OF THIS SUPPRESSION IS NARROW (Law 1) - the following remain REPORTABLE at full severity and are NOT covered: (a) any path where the pot leaves without the caller paying for nudgeSize real mints; (b) any path where refund > paymentAmount; (c) any path where a NON-QUALIFYING batch extracts pot-sized value (a recurrence of yield-claim-nft d06e3191.../ycn19h1 or phoenix 2d34673536...); (d) the aggregate over-funding class (858e9e80..., and the run-22 sigma-pots Medium), which is about the pot being too LARGE relative to cost - a different claim from the comparison being easy.

KI #16 - ACCEPTED SUBSIDY RATE (owner, 2026-07-26) - DO NOT FILE: 'the nudge pot exceeds the cost of one qualifying batch' is a SUBSIDY RATE, NOT A VALUE LEAK. FUNDING-SOURCE REASONING: the protocol owns its capital and earns yield on it from external vaults (e.g. Tokemak); that yield funds phlimbo and the nudge pot. The pot is yield on protocol-owned principal - never principal, never user deposits. So over-topping the pot costs the protocol OPPORTUNITY (the yield could have gone straight to liquidity growth), not value. It is an accepted short-run marketing spend: a visible profit opportunity pulls users in and the deficit closes as the lowest-bidding marginal user snipes the mint; NudgeStreamer meters release so the market finds a clearing price. A LARGE POT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING. Empirically the pot has never once reached even 50% of the qualifying cost before someone minted. DO NOT FILE, in any severity or framing: 'pot > nudgeSize * price is profitable', 'the count-only gate is value-blind', 'the payout should be bounded by what the batch actually paid', 'the qualifying cost is recycled so the claim is repeatable', 'aggregate/whitelist-sum pots exceed one qualifying cost', or 'NudgeStreamer fails to cap the payout'. *** CARVE-OUTS - THESE REMAIN FULLY REPORTABLE (Law 1; this suppression must NOT widen): (a) any path where the pot leaves WITHOUT the caller paying for nudgeSize real mints; (b) any path where refund > paymentAmount; (c) any path where a NON-QUALIFYING batch extracts pot-sized value (recurrence of yield-claim-nft d06e3191... / ycn19h1 or phoenix 2d34673536...); (d) ANY CLAIMANT TAKING OTHER USERS' MONEY. The suppression covers only PROTOCOL-DIRECTED INCENTIVE FUNDS SOURCED FROM EXTERNALLY-DERIVED YIELD. Value that originated with other callers - notably forfeited sub-DUST_THRESHOLD refund residue accreting into the pot (run-25 M-03, ledger 38ea47b14ce3...) - is NOT protocol incentive money and remains reportable at honest (small) severity. Carve-outs (a)/(b)/(c) mirror KI #15's and were VERIFIED CLEAN by run-25. *** CORRECTION TO KI #15 CARVE-OUT (d): run-25 read KI #15's 'aggregate over-funding' carve-out TOO BROADLY. KI #15 (d) is about ACCIDENTAL over-funding (the owner mis-sizing a transfer), NOT about a DELIBERATELY-SET SUBSIDY RATE. A pot that is large because the owner chose the subsidy rate is covered by THIS entry and must not be re-filed under KI #15 (d). Run-25's M-01 (96823199d298...) and M-02 (c7a410602b29...) were withdrawn on exactly this ground - do not re-derive them.
designDecisions: Variable-runway / owner-set APY target emission model: owner sets target APY, contract derives R = S * A / SECONDS_PER_YEAR, runway V/R is a derived quantity
S = totalStaked * latestPrice (staked-subset notional), not aggregate minted notional T - audit M-03 fix

latestPrice = price / r where r = 1 + growthBasisPoints/10_000; price from nftMinter.configs(dispatcherIndex) is the NEXT mint price, dividing by r recovers the most-recent paid price; growthBasisPoints == 0 collapses latestPrice to price
Pull-on-interaction: every stake/unstake/claim first calls _syncBudget which invokes pull() on the configured dispatcher hook to sweep outstanding mint debt
V = balance + mintDebt (balance plus pending phUSD at the dispatcher hook)
Solvency invariant: balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt holds at ALL times

stake/unstake invoke _recomputeSchedule AFTER totalStaked mutation (in addition to head-of-function _syncBudget recompute at OLD totalStaked); claim does NOT need tail recompute since totalStaked unchanged
setTargetAPY settles accrual at OLD rate via _updatePool() before mutating targetAPY
MAX_TARGET_APY = 0.5e18 (50% APY ceiling)
Share unit = NFT units staked (ERC1155 balances), NOT ERC20 wei

Single-ID ERC1155 staking; ERC1155 contract address is immutable constructor arg; token ID is owner-settable via setStakedId only while totalStaked == 0 (accommodates NFTMinter reconfiguration like Balancer pool migration)
All reward math uses OZ Math.mulDiv with floor rounding (conservative for reward contract)

Payment token MAY be a nudge-whitelisted token (owner decision 2026-07-25, docs/phoenix-nft-staking-payment-token-as-nudge-token-plan.md). Safety comes from accounting, not from exclusion: the caller's budget is tracked in memory and is the SOLE source of the refund (never balanceOf), the minter allowance is held at the exact next mint price and re-asserted ABSOLUTELY every iteration (idempotent for tokens that decrement allowance, corrective for those that do not), the reward snapshot is taken BEFORE the payment pull so it reads the uncontaminated pot, and the refund happens BEFORE the payout. TWO ORDERING CONSTRAINTS ARE LOAD-BEARING and must survive any refactor: (1) snapshot before pull - moving it after would make the payout P+A and eat the refund; (2) refund before payout. The runtime payment-token skip in _snapshotRewards and the admin-time rejection in setNudgeTokenWhitelist are REMOVED/RELAXED as a result - their absence is intentional, not a missing guard.

Nudge pot size is a SUBSIDY RATE, not an invariant (owner, 2026-07-26). The count-only qualifying gate (`qualifies = _nudgeSize != 0 && count >= _nudgeSize`) paying the accumulated pot to a qualifying batcher IS THE MECHANISM, deliberately so - it is how the incentive is delivered and how price discovery happens. The pot is funded from externally-derived yield on protocol-owned capital (see systemAssumptions 'NUDGE-POT FUNDING SOURCE'), so a pot exceeding one qualifying batch's cost is an accepted short-run marketing cost, closed by the lowest-bidding marginal user. NudgeStreamer is the metering device for that price discovery - it is a TIMING THROTTLE, not a value cap, and its not being a value cap is INTENDED, not a missing guard. The docs' 'by construction it is a fraction of the cost' phrasing (docs/multi-token-nudge.md:56-60, :299-302) is a DOCUMENTATION DEFECT to be restated as a subsidy policy - it is NOT a request for a code-enforced bound (see ledger 75305ec0... / a7dffb34...).
systemAssumptions: yield-claim-nft sibling submodule's BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook is the source of mint-debt - this staker must be set as the hook's recipient
nftMinter.configs(dispatcherIndex) returns a struct with .price (next mint price) and .growthBasisPoints fields
phUSD is the single reward token; minted by the dispatcher hook on pull()
Global Pauser (from pauser submodule) is the only address allowed to pause/unpause via IPausable
Mutable siblings (lib/mutable/) expose interfaces only - never reach into implementations
OpenZeppelin used for all standard primitives (Ownable, Pausable, ReentrancyGuard, ERC1155 receiver, SafeERC20) - custom reimplementations prohibited

NUDGE-POT FUNDING SOURCE (owner correction, 2026-07-26) - READ THIS BEFORE RATING ANY NUDGE-POT FINDING. Across the Phoenix suite the protocol OWNS its capital and earns YIELD on it from external vaults (e.g. Tokemak). That externally-derived yield is what flows to phlimbo and to the BatchNFTMinter / BatchNFTMinterMultiToken nudge pot. The pot is therefore funded by YIELD ON PROTOCOL-OWNED PRINCIPAL - never by principal itself, and never by user deposits. CONSEQUENCE FOR SEVERITY: if the pot is topped beyond the cost of the qualifying mints, the protocol's loss is OPPORTUNITY COST (that yield could instead have gone straight into liquidity growth), NOT ECONOMIC LOSS. Do NOT model this as the shape an auditor reflexively assumes (owner puts up principal and only a fraction returns) - that shape is WRONG here and has produced at least one withdrawn Medium (run-25 M-01, 96823199d298..., withdrawn 2026-07-26). The over-top is a DELIBERATE SUBSIDY RATE and a MARKETING SPEND: a visible profit opportunity pulls users in, and the deficit closes as the lowest-bidding marginal user snipes the mint. NudgeStreamer meters release precisely so the market finds a clearing price - a large pot is the mechanism WORKING, not a failure. EMPIRICAL: in live operation the pot has NEVER ONCE reached even 50% of the qualifying cost before someone minted. SCOPE OF THIS ASSUMPTION IS NARROW (Law 1): it justifies only payouts of PROTOCOL-DIRECTED INCENTIVE FUNDS SOURCED FROM EXTERNALLY-DERIVED YIELD. It does NOT bless a claimant taking OTHER USERS' MONEY (e.g. forfeited sub-DUST_THRESHOLD refunds accreting into the pot - run-25 M-03's channel, 38ea47b14ce3..., which remains reportable at honest/small severity), and it does NOT bless any path where the pot leaves WITHOUT the caller paying for nudgeSize real mints, where refund > paymentAmount, or where a NON-QUALIFYING batch extracts pot-sized value. See knownIssues KI #16 for the full carve-out list.
